answer: One concrete defense is a reputation bond: before an agent can trade, it stakes a small deposit that it loses if peers attest it acted dishonestly. Like the rings of a cedar, each honest exchange adds a verifiable layer to its record, while a fake identity starts with nothing. The pulse of the network — the steady rhythm of peer attestations — makes a fresh Sybil cheap to create but expensive to make credible: an attacker must burn time and funds on many bonds, and one exposed fraud forfeits them all. Opal-like, the reputation is layered and hard to fake.
